questions.prompt: A loop registers three click handlers: `for (var i = 0; i < 3; i++) { buttons[i].onclick = () => alert(i); }`. Every button alerts 3. Why, and how would you fix it?

rubric.text: explains that var is function-scoped, so all three handlers close over the same single i
proposes a working fix: let (a fresh binding per iteration), an IIFE, or passing i as an argument
explains that the handlers run after the loop has finished, when i is already 3

questions.prompt: A React component sets up `setInterval(() => console.log(count), 1000)` inside `useEffect(..., [])`. As the user clicks, count goes up on screen, but the log always prints 0. Why, and what would you change?

rubric.text: identifies a stale closure: the interval callback captured count from the first render
proposes a working fix: add count to the dependency array, read it from a ref, or use a functional update
mentions clearing the interval in the effect's cleanup

answers.question: q-loop
answers.answer: var is function scoped, so there is only one i shared by every handler. By the time anyone clicks, the loop has finished and i is 3. Changing var to let fixes it because let creates a new binding for each iteration.

answers.question: q-loop
answers.answer: Use let instead of var and it works.

answers.question: q-loop
answers.answer: All the arrow functions reference the same variable i because var isn't block scoped. Wrap the body in an IIFE that takes i as a parameter so each handler gets its own copy.

answers.question: q-loop
answers.answer: The onclick runs later, after the loop is done, so it sees the final value. I am not sure how to fix it, maybe use setTimeout?

answers.question: q-loop
answers.answer: JavaScript arrays start at zero so buttons[3] is out of bounds and alert shows the length. Fix it by looping to 2 instead.

answers.question: q-interval
answers.answer: The effect only runs once because of the empty dependency array, so the interval's callback closed over count from the first render, which was 0 — a stale closure. Add count to the dependencies so the effect re-runs, and return a cleanup that calls clearInterval so the old interval stops.

answers.question: q-interval
answers.answer: It's a stale closure: the callback captured the first render's count. Keep the latest count in a useRef and log countRef.current instead.

answers.question: q-interval
answers.answer: You need to clear the interval when the component unmounts, otherwise it leaks.

answers.question: q-interval
answers.answer: console.log is asynchronous in React, so it prints before the state updates. Use console.info instead.

answers.question: q-interval
answers.answer: Because the empty array means the effect saw count only once, when it was 0, and never again. Put count in the dependency array.
